title: Audiological manifestations of Fabry disease in South Korea: A single-center cohort study on hearing impairment and tinnitus
content:
by Hae Jin Oh, Jae Hyuk Choi, Seok-Hyun Kim, Il-Woo Lee, Hyun Min Lee, Chong Kun Cheon

Fabry disease (FD), a rare X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by α-galactosidase A deficiency, leads to progressive accumulation of globotriaosylceramide and globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) in various tissues. Hearing loss has been reported in FD internationally; however, data on Korean patients are lacking. This retrospective study investigated the prevalence and characteristics of hearing loss and tinnitus in 34 patients with FD who underwent pure-tone audiometry at a single tertiary medical center in South Korea between May 2008 and April 2023. Hearing loss was defined using two criteria: a four-frequency average (4FA) > 25 dB HL or a threshold > 25 dB HL at any measured frequency. Associations between hearing thresholds and clinical variables were examined using exploratory linear regression adjusted for age. Among the 34 patients (7 males and 27 females; mean age at the first otolaryngology visit, 35.8 ± 18.3 years), the mean 4FA was 15.57 ± 15.00 dB HL. Hearing loss was identified in 17.6% of patients by the 4FA criterion and in 52.9% by the single-frequency criterion, predominantly involving high frequencies. Older age groups had higher hearing thresholds across all frequency ranges (all p < 0.01), whereas phenotype, GLA variant type, and plasma lyso-Gb3 level were not associated with hearing thresholds. Tinnitus was reported by 52.9% of patients, and in exploratory age-adjusted analyses, patients with tinnitus had higher hearing thresholds than those without. In the longitudinal analysis (n = 18), the mean annual change in 4FA was 0.37 ± 0.76 dB/year, and no factor was significantly associated with the rate of change. Older age was associated with higher hearing thresholds; however, without age-matched controls, the contribution of FD could not be distinguished from that of age-related hearing loss. Given the small sample size, these findings are preliminary but consistent with existing recommendations for regular audiological evaluation in patients with FD.
